subject: Real-time endpoint: intermittent lag — customer bridge & next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@pinefin.com>, PineFin SRE <sre@pinefin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Real-time endpoint: intermittent lag — customer bridge & next steps

Hi Marta / PineFin SRE team,

Thanks again for flagging the slowdowns you observed this morning on the /v1/streams endpoint (session IDs listed in the trace you sent). We ran an initial triage and want to: 1) confirm what we saw, 2) put in short-term mitigations you can apply immediately, and 3) schedule a technical bridge with our SREs to walk through traces and follow up with a post-incident summary.

What we observed so far:
- A burst of elevated p99 token latency affecting streaming connections between 08:35–08:55 PDT.
- Correlated KV-cache misses on a subset of nodes and a brief autoscaler latency while new workers were provisioned.
- No customer data exposure; this is a performance incident only.

Immediate mitigations (apply now):
- If feasible, switch streaming clients to the non-streaming fallback for critical flows: POST /v1/generate with smaller max_tokens for the next 30m.
- Enable client-side chunked retries: retry partial chunk requests with exponential backoff (100ms -> 400ms) before reopening the stream.
- Add a small jitter (50–150ms) to connection start to avoid synchronized reconnections during recovery windows.

We're ready to run a short bridge at 10:00 PDT to walk traces and apply temporary routing rules. If that doesn't work for your team, we're flexible on timing — propose a slot.

Attachments: latency-trace-20250618.png (trace snippet), bridge_runbook_v2.pdf (recommended temporary settings).

Apologies for the disruption — we know real-time UX matters and will keep you updated.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attached: bridge_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook excerpt)
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@pinefin.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Real-time endpoint: intermittent lag — customer bridge & next steps

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the fast response. We applied the non-streaming fallback for the payments-notifs flow and saw immediate improvement.

10:00 PDT for the bridge works for us — will have our lead SRE (Carlos) on the call and we've uploaded our longer trace file (sensitive) to the SRE channel.

Notes from our side:
- The user impact was primarily in mobile sessions (iOS app) between 08:30–09:00.
- We saw elevated reconnects and some duplicated token emissions on reconnect.

See you on the bridge.

—Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform, PineFin
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal notes: PineFin bridge recap and immediate work items

(Internal) Quick recap from the 10:00 PDT bridge with PineFin:
- Confirmed high p99 due to a combination of cold KV-cache misses and a short delay (50–120s) in our autoscaler launching new serving pods under a particular instance type.
- Root cause: an edge rolling update unintentionally reduced available warm workers in us-west-2; the autoscaler then hit a provisioning latency window while capacity was re-balanced.

Action items we committed to during the call:
1) Deploy a targeted hotfix to avoid simultaneous edge rollouts in the same AZ (INF-4219).
2) Ship an autoscaler config tweak to reduce scale-up probe interval from 45s -> 15s for streaming pools (deploy staged today).
3) Provide a post-incident package for PineFin with: detailed traces, adjusted runbook, and temporary client settings they applied.

I've opened INF-4219 and attached the trace snippet to the ticket. Olga — can you own the autoscaler config change and the staged rollout? I'll coordinate the customer communication and the postmortem doc.

-Karthik
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@pinefin.com>, PineFin SRE <sre@pinefin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: incident summary, mitigations applied, and recommended client config

Hi Marta / Carlos,

Thanks again for your patience and for joining the bridge. Per our commitments, here's a concise post-incident summary and concrete next steps.

Summary:
- Window: 2025-06-18 08:35–08:55 PDT
- Impact: intermittent increased p99 latency for streaming endpoints (observed across mobile and web UX).
- Root cause: targeted edge rollout in us-west-2 reduced the pool of warm streaming workers while autoscaler probe interval was too long, creating a provisioning gap.

What we changed (platform):
- Hotfix deployed to sequencing controller to serialize rollouts in the same AZ (INF-4219).
- Autoscaler probe interval reduced to 15s for streaming pools; staged rollout completed in us-west-2 and will be rolled globally after validation.
- Improved telemetry added to detect KV-cache miss hotspots and trigger pre-warming.

Recommended client settings (for PineFin immediate use):
- Fallback: temporarily use POST /v1/generate for critical flows where streaming UX is optional.
- Chunk retries: implement 3 retries for partial chunk failures with initial backoff 100ms and jitter 50–150ms.
- Connection jitter: add randomized 50–150ms delay before reconnect attempts to avoid thundering herds.

Attachments provided: bridge_runbook_v2.pdf (updated with the client settings above), latency-trace-20250618.png (annotated), and our internal incident timeline.

Next steps and timelines:
- 2025-06-20: complete global autoscaler config rollout if validation in us-west-2 is green.
- 2025-06-22: share formal postmortem (root cause analysis + action backlog) and invite PineFin to review for any additional remediation priorities.

If you'd like a dedicated change window for applying client-side fallbacks, let us know and we'll coordinate to minimize user-facing impact.

Apologies again for the interruption — we'll continue monitoring your traffic and notify you proactively if we see any anomalies.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
